topic: Deep Research Agent with Citation Tracking & Conflict Detection

recommendation.reason: Your current AG2 implementation is a minimal wrapper. Multiple open-source projects provide the specific citation tracking, conflict detection, and workflow features you need. Adapting one of these is faster and more reliable than building from scratch.
recommendation.reusableOption: tarun7r/deep-research-agent (LangGraph-based with citation backing and credibility scoring) or Agents365-ai/scholar-deep-research (8-phase pipeline with citation chasing)
recommendation.biggestUnknown: None of the surveyed open-source tools explicitly demonstrate conflict detection across contradicting sources in their current releases. ConflictRAG research framework exists but requires integration work.

notableDesigns.title: Multi-agent collaboration
notableDesigns.detail: Four specialized agents work together: each handles different research phases (planning, searching, analyzing, synthesizing). This division of labor enables more thorough coverage than single-agent approaches.

notableDesigns.title: Credibility scoring
notableDesigns.detail: Assigns quality metrics to sources and claims, helping users assess reliability. Critical for investment memos where source trustworthiness matters.

notableDesigns.title: LangGraph state management
notableDesigns.detail: Uses LangGraph's checkpoint system for stateful workflows, enabling pause/resume and human-in-the-loop interventions during long research runs.

reusableLessons: Multi-agent architecture with specialized roles improves research depth and coverage
Citation backing must be built into the agent workflow, not added as post-processing
LangGraph checkpointing provides resumability without custom state management code
Credibility scoring helps prioritize sources but doesn't replace explicit conflict detection

notableDesigns.title: 8-phase literature review pipeline
notableDesigns.detail: Structured workflow: Discovery → Ranking → Retrieval → Citation chasing → Analysis → Self-critique → Synthesis → Reporting. Each phase has specific quality gates.

notableDesigns.title: Citation chasing
notableDesigns.detail: Automatically follows references and citations to discover canonical papers and related work. Addresses the synthesis gap where agents miss ~79% of expert-cited papers.

notableDesigns.title: Per-paper audit trail
notableDesigns.detail: Enforced citation anchoring ensures every claim traces back to a specific paper with verifiable provenance. Critical for academic and investment research integrity.

notableDesigns.title: Federated source deduplication
notableDesigns.detail: Queries multiple academic databases and deduplicates across them, maximizing coverage while avoiding redundant processing.

reusableLessons: 8-phase pipeline structure provides clear quality gates and intermediate checkpoints
Citation chasing dramatically improves coverage beyond initial search results
Per-paper audit trails are essential for rigorous evidence-based research
Self-critique mechanisms reduce but don't eliminate hallucinated citations
Academic focus means adapting to general web research requires work
competitors.summary: Best citation infrastructure and academic rigor. Specialized for literature review; would need adaptation for general web research and explicit conflict reporting.
competitors.coverageNote: GitHub anonymous API used; project documentation and homepage verified.

competitors.name: ConflictRAG (Research Framework)
competitors.overview: Academic framework for conflict-aware retrieval-augmented generation. Detects, classifies, and resolves knowledge conflicts across sources before generating answers. Achieves 88.7% conflict-detection F1 score in research evaluation.

comparison.candidate: Not focused: Framework addresses conflict detection, not citation management
Native (research): 88.7% F1 score detecting conflicts; requires implementation work
Not applicable: Component library, not end-to-end system
Not applicable: Provides conflict analysis, not report generation
Research framework; integration required

notableDesigns.title: Conflict detection pipeline
notableDesigns.detail: Three stages: (1) Detect conflicting statements across retrieved sources (2) Classify conflict type (contradiction, partial overlap, perspective difference) (3) Resolve or surface conflicts before generation.

notableDesigns.title: Dual-perspective retrieval
notableDesigns.detail: Collects evidence for both original claims and their negations, ensuring both supporting and contradicting information is captured. Prevents one-sided synthesis.

notableDesigns.title: 88.7% F1 detection accuracy
notableDesigns.detail: Research evaluation shows high reliability in identifying genuine conflicts vs. compatible differences. Critical for investment memo accuracy.

reusableLessons: Conflict detection must happen before synthesis, not as post-processing
Dual-perspective retrieval (claim + negation) is more effective than single-direction search
Classifying conflict types (contradiction vs. perspective) helps users understand disagreements
Research framework requires significant engineering to integrate into production system
No open-source implementation available; would need to build from paper descriptions

notableDesigns.title: Automatic state snapshots
notableDesigns.detail: Saves graph state at every node transition without manual checkpointing code. Enables pause/resume with no additional engineering.

notableDesigns.title: Thread-based isolation
notableDesigns.detail: Each research session gets a unique thread_id. Pass the same ID to resume exactly where it stopped. Multiple concurrent sessions stay separate.

notableDesigns.title: Multiple storage backends
notableDesigns.detail: Supports in-memory, file-based, and database checkpointers. Choose persistence level based on reliability needs.

reusableLessons: Framework-level checkpointing is more reliable than manual state management
Thread-based isolation essential for concurrent research sessions
Any LangGraph agent automatically gains resumability when compiled with a checkpointer
Consider tarun7r/deep-research-agent as it already uses LangGraph checkpointing
